title: [RFC Feedback] IFC5-014 — Evidence: working dual-representation prototype, answers to Q1 and Q2
author: louistrue
raw_text:
Comment type: Evidence

RFC-014 §8 asks for a prototype showing Hello Wall with both parametric and tessellated representations plus a round-trip to IFC4.x. I have been building that. Offering it as evidence, not as an alternative proposal.

Geometry is carried in three tiers: procedural (profiles, extrusion, revolution, boolean), explicit Brep topology, and a triangulated display mesh. The highest tier present is authoritative; everything below is a derived cache. The mesh is used for display when present but never becomes the source of truth for its own source. Each node type has a JSON schema. Input is real IFC4 SPF: the STEP parser extracts IfcExtrudedAreaSolid with its IfcArbitraryClosedProfileDef, and GlobalIds are preserved as node identity through to the tiered output.

Q1 — are the meshes authoritative or derived? Here they are derived, and the marking is machine-checkable rather than conventional. A derived mesh carries a canonical content hash of its source: RFC 8785 JCS canonicalisation plus SHA-256, written sha256-<hex>. A consumer resolves a cached mesh to fresh, stale or unknown. Changing a profile dimension or moving a source vertex flips the same cached mesh from fresh to stale; permuting key order in the source does not; a mesh with no hash reports unknown rather than being assumed fresh.

This is the row I think the §5 tradeoff table is missing. The stated risk of §4.3 dual representation is that the two copies disagree. With a source hash the disagreement is detectable by the receiver, without re-deriving the geometry and without trusting the producer. Without it, dual representation means two sources of truth and a convention. My suggestion: whichever of §4.2 or §4.3 is chosen, require derived geometry to carry a hash of its source. RFC-006 Q1 asks whether canonical serialization is required and already cites RFC 8785; this is one concrete thing it buys.

Q2 — must receivers distinguish design-intent from visualization geometry? Here they must, and can do so without parsing geometry. Tiers live in separate tables, a consumer declares which tiers it wants, and the resolver logs every table access, so 'a conformant mesh-only consumer reads no other tier's table' is observable rather than promised. That is testable in implementation-independent form: it constrains what a receiver may read, not how it is built.

The cost is real. Splitting tiers across tables means a node's geometry is not readable without the index and the loader, which loses the schema-free parseability RFC-036 §4.5 argues for. That is a genuine tension between §4.3 and RFC-036 and I do not think it can be designed away, only chosen.

On §4.1: both current examples carry mesh-only geometry. IFC4X geometry is predominantly procedural, so mesh-first is lossy by construction rather than by degree, and the customdata migration aid preserves the bytes without the meaning. This bears on RFC-018 Q4 and on absorbed Topic 17 in RFC-007, 'which information is authoritative when semantic and mesh geometry disagree', which the tier ordering above is one concrete answer to.

Q3 and Q4 are handled in the prototype but not in a form I would put forward as evidence yet.

Limits: this runs on our own post-alpha variant with external attribute tables, not on upstream IFCX, so it shows satisfiability, not conformance. Every claim above is backed by a named passing test and I can link them. Procedural coverage is extrusion, revolution and boolean; NURBS and general CSG exist as evidence the interface holds, not as robust implementations. Scale is undemonstrated — cubes and one wall, no performance data, which is a gap against RFC-034.

Happy to prepare a Hello Wall variant in whatever shape is most useful for the committee comparison.

Branches with prototype: https://github.com/LTplus-AG/IFCX/tree/louistrue-geometry-tiers and https://github.com/LTplus-AG/IFCX/tree/louistrue-mesh-core
